clauses.gap: No source read shows that the national emergency proclaimed by Proc. 2914 ended, which is the event the order's expiry depends on; no instrument read names the order as revoked, superseded or terminated. Candidates: Pub. L. 94-412 sec. 101 (powers terminated 1978-09-14) and the repeal of 10 U.S.C. 5231-5234 by Pub. L. 96-513 effective 1981-09-15.

gaps.what: Evidence that the national emergency proclaimed by Proc. 2914 ended, and when. This is the event the order's own expiry clause depends on. Pub. L. 94-412 sec. 101 terminates powers and authorities, not in terms the emergency, and does not name the order.
gaps.where_to_look: A proclamation, statute or official compilation note stating that the Proc. 2914 emergency ended; the notes to 50 U.S.C. 1601; the Proc. 2914 entry in the OFR proclamation disposition tables

gaps.what: Whether the 1977 and 1978 amendments to section 5231 (Pub. L. 95-79 sec. 811(b); Pub. L. 95-485 sec. 818(a)) changed the suspended 5231(b) number limits before 1981. Not read. The U.S. Code note confirms only that those acts amended section 5231.

Whether the repeal of the suspended section and of the suspension authority, by a statute that does not name the order, counts as an ending under the project rules. Recorded as a candidate, not as an ending.
gaps.where_to_look: Project rules on general statutes that do not name the order; Pub. L. 96-513 secs. 331 and 701 (94 Stat. 2896); transition provisions in sec. 601 et seq.

moves.note: Federal Register printing 25 FR 8633 held as OCR text (re-read in this repair); operative words legible; one operative clause.

OPEN, not NO. The order expires under its own terms on June 30 of the fiscal year after the Proc. 2914 emergency ends, but no held or opened source shows that the emergency ended. Pub. L. 94-412 terminates powers and authorities, with savings provisions, and names neither the emergency nor the order. Pub. L. 96-513 repealed 10 U.S.C. 5231-5234 without naming the order, so it is recorded as a candidate only. No positive current source supports YES.

The single clause has a state: open, with the missing fact named (evidence that the Proc. 2914 emergency ended, or an instrument naming the order). If an open clause does not satisfy T4 under project practice, the tier is T3.

The OFR 1989 disposition table, the only source said to name the order as terminated, was not opened because the slice gives no file path. After that, evidence of the order's stated expiry event is still needed.

propositions.claim: The order was issued under 10 U.S.C. 5234 and printed in the Federal Register of 8 Sept. 1960.
propositions.quote: By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 5234 of title 10 of the United States Code, it is ordered as follows

propositions.claim: The only command suspends the 5231(b) limits on the number of admirals and vice admirals.
propositions.quote: relate to the number of officers serving in the grades of admiral and vice admiral are hereby suspended

propositions.claim: The suspension carries its own end date, tied to the end of the 1950 national emergency. The text does not show that this event occurred.
propositions.quote: until June 30 of the fiscal year following that in which the national emergency proclaimed by Proclamation No. 2914 of December 16, 1950, shall end

propositions.claim: The National Emergencies Act terminated, as of 14 Sept. 1978, the powers and authorities held as a result of any national emergency declaration in effect on 14 Sept. 1976, subject to savings provisions for pending actions, actions based on prior acts, and matured rights or duties. It names neither the Proc. 2914 emergency nor this order and does not in terms end the emergency. Candidate only.
propositions.quote: as a result of the existence of any declaration of national emergency in effect on September 14, 1976, are terminated two years from September 14, 1976. Such termination shall not affect— (1) any action taken or proceeding pending not finally concluded or determined on such date; (2) any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to such date; or (3) any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date.

review.conclusion_reason: The asserted own-terms ending lacks evidence that the specified emergency ended. Neither cited general statute names the order, so the audit rules prohibit treating them alone as proof of its ending. The claimed 1981 outer bound is consequently unsupported. The separate formal-status assertion is not independently established by this limited record.
missed_evidence: The opened 50 U.S.C. 1601(a), https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/1601, includes savings provisions for prior actions, proceedings, and matured rights or duties. These qualify the worker's broad description but do not establish this order's termination.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (HELD_UNROUTED fits the supplied slice's uninspected OFR disposition-table lead). The rules already resolve the proposed general-statute inference; the immediate evidentiary obstacle is obtaining the underlying table, followed by evidence establishing the order's specified expiry event, rather than a NEEDS_RULING question.
review.suspected_defect: The conclusion converts general statutory termination of powers and an alleged statutory repeal into an own-terms ending, despite expressly acknowledging that the emergency's ending is unproved and neither statute names the order.
